references.text: The priest shall examine the skin disease, and this establishes the priest's role in assessing skin diseases and purity.
Describes white spots on the skin and the priest's examination of them in connection with leprosy.
The priest declares the person clean after a new examination, parallel to the declaration of cleanliness in verse 17.
The priest declares the person clean when all the skin has turned white, showing that whiteness can indicate purity.
The priest goes out to examine whether the disease is healed, and this follows up the cleansing process.
Miriam becomes as white as snow from leprosy, showing the connection between whiteness and skin disease.
Naaman's leprosy that turns as white as snow shows the contrast between sickness and healing.
Jesus heals a leper and sends him to the priest to be declared clean, in accordance with the Mosaic Law.
Jesus sends the lepers to the priests, and they are cleansed on the way, in line with the law's regulations concerning cleansing.
